facts.location: Form CRS, "What fees will I pay?"
facts.quote: If you place a trade, you will pay a commission or transaction fee in some cases. There can also be expenses built into the trade price or the investment itself.

facts.display: Recommendations are available if you want advice, but Schwab does not manage or monitor brokerage accounts.
facts.quote: We offer investment and account recommendations if you would like advice. … We do not manage or monitor your brokerage accounts.

facts.display: Schwab earns a "spread" on cash in your account: the difference between what it earns on that cash and the interest it pays you.
facts.location: Form CRS, how the firm makes money
facts.quote: The “spread” on cash in your accounts—i.e., the difference between what we earn and what we pay you in interest.

facts.display: Phone: 800-435-4000 (listed in Form CRS). Support hours were not verified.
facts.location: Form CRS, "Where can I find additional information?"
facts.quote: To request a copy of this relationship summary, call 800-435-4000.

facts.reason: Firm-specific requirements were not verified. Every broker-dealer must collect your name, date of birth, address and taxpayer identification number; see the identity verification guide.
Promotions change often and are not shown or used in comparisons. Check the firm's own site for current offers and their terms.

facts.display: Earns money from third parties and affiliates on cash, mutual funds and ETFs in your account, which gives it an incentive to encourage those products.
facts.location: Form CRS, "What fees will I pay?"
facts.quote: We earn money from third parties and affiliates on certain products, including cash, mutual funds, and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) held in your account(s), so we have an incentive to encourage investment in those products.
